definitions.canForceLife: P can force the game into a position containing a Benson-alive P chain, against any opposition. Boolean reachability game; least attractor of the position-target over the basic-ko move graph with P-side existential / opponent-side universal states. passes=1 pass edges are losing sinks (two passes end the game); implemented as remaining=outdeg+1 for universal passes=1 states.
definitions.vertex_space_3x3_4x4: WZO2 table entries (reachable-from-empty closure under basic ko, passes in {0,1}; passes=2 terminal states omitted). Child closure verified: 0 placement misses, 0 pass misses at both sizes.
definitions.vertex_space_2x2_3x2_4x3: reachable-from-empty closure built by BFS under the same basic-ko move relation (no WZO2 table exists).
definitions.L_H_source: 3x3/4x4: the WZO2 entries (verified). 2x2/3x2/4x3: the generic loopy fixpoint implemented in src/t394_force_life.zig (exp6_solve.zig semantics, ADR-0020), calibrated against the WZO2 3x3 table per-entry (0 mismatches over 49,428) and the committed roots ([−4,+4], [−6,+6]).

T1.statement: empty-board root is decisive iff canForceLife holds for some player at the root
T1.result: HOLDS in the L==H (single-valued) form at all five sizes: 2x2 [−4,+4] not single + no life-forcing; 3x2 [−6,+6] same; 3x3 [+9] single + Black can force life; 4x3 [4,12] not single + none; 4x4 [1,16] not single + none. FAILS in the non-straddling (L>0) form at 4x3 and 4x4: the root is decisive for Black (L=+4, L=+1) yet NO player can force a Benson-alive chain. The brief's prediction (canForceLife holds for Black at 3x3 AND 4x4) is falsified at 4x4; my timestamped 4x3 prediction (true) is falsified at 4x3. The operator's territory-denial phrasing is false: on 4x3/4x4 neither player can force unconditional life, yet the game is decisive for Black by area.
T1.cuts: against the operator's hypothesis at 4x3/4x4: territory (area) can be won without any Benson-alive group; the game does not loop merely because life cannot be forced.

T2.statement: every draw-by-loop entry (L<=0<=H) has canForceLife false for both players
T2.result: HOLDS EXACTLY at 2x2 (92/92), 3x2 (298/298), 3x3 (1,248/1,248 — the brief's number reproduced). FAILS at 4x3 (32/26,520 = 0.12%) and 4x4 (9,376/895,216 = 1.05%): exceptions are states where a player can force life yet the bracket still straddles zero — the forcible territory is too small to decide. Witnesses and reachable-alive areas in the size entries.
T2.cuts: mostly for the operator's hypothesis (a sound draw-oracle at <=3x3), with a small measured exception rate at 4x3/4x4 that bounds its certification value.

T3.statement: among states where neither can force life, what fraction are draw-by-loop vs decisive?
T3.result: the neither-can-force-life class is mostly DECISIVE at every size >= 3x2: 2x2 16/124 (12.9%), 3x2 242/608 (39.8%), 3x3 7,396/12,804 (57.8%), 4x3 223,074/315,762 (70.7%), 4x4 19,518,338/22,885,430 (85.3%). Large decisive mass sits in the neither class: territory-denial does NOT explain those wins.
T3.cuts: against the operator's hypothesis: the 'neither can force life => draw' implication is false — decisive wins happen without either player being able to force unconditional life.

verdict.landmark: advances L2 (proven 4×4 values): the canForceLife instrument is certified (controls, verification, calibrations all green) and shows the draw-by-loop region at 4x4 (895,216 entries) is 98.95% clean of life-forcing, with 9,376 exceptions (1.05%) carrying witnesses. As a pruning oracle the classifier is sound where T2 holds exactly (<=3x3) and has a measured, witness-carrying exception rate at 4x3/4x4. Cost: the Boolean pass at 4x4 was ~61s at ~3.3 GB peak vs the ~1h value iteration — two orders of magnitude cheaper.

new_rows.claim: **The empty-board root is single-valued (L==H) if and only if some player can force a Benson-alive chain — holds at all five solved sizes (5/5).** 2x2 [-4,+4] not single, neither can force; 3x2 [-6,+6] not single, neither; 3x3 [+9] single, Black CAN force; 4x3 [4,12] not single, neither; 4x4 [1,16] not single, neither. Read carefully: forcible unconditional life buys **rule-independence** (a single score that cannot depend on the cycle rule), NOT victory. **The operator's territory-denial phrasing is FALSIFIED at 4x3 and 4x4:** those roots are decisive for Black on area (L=+4, L=+1) although NEITHER player can force a Benson-alive chain — so decisive wins demonstrably do not require forcible immortality. Operator's loss; cuts toward 'unconditional life is the wrong notion of territory for decisive wins'. Both the brief's 4x4 prediction and the worker's timestamped 4x3 prediction were falsified by measurement. **SCOPE:** measured, single instrument (src/t394_force_life.zig), Boolean attractor over the basic-ko move graph with a Benson-alive target set; the 4x3 root [4,12] is MEASURED and NOT independently audited — do not cite it as solved until a second seat verifies it.

**Draw-by-loop states are CONFINED to the neither-can-force-life class — exactly through 3x3, and with measured exceptions above it.** draw-by-loop (L<=0<=H) implies neither player can force a Benson-alive chain: 0 exceptions at 2x2 (92), 3x2 (298) and 3x3 (1,248); 32 exceptions at 4x3 (99.88% hold); **9,376 exceptions at 4x4 of 895,216 (98.95% hold)**, each carrying a witness record (colex, side, ko, passes, L, H, cfB, cfW, alive area). **EXPLICIT NON-CLAIM — the converse is FALSE and must never be inferred from this row:** canForceLife=false-for-both is NOT a draw certificate. Its error rate is governed by GLOBAL.NEITHER-FORCE-MOSTLY-DECISIVE (85.3% of that class is decisive at 4x4), not by this row's 1.05% exception rate. Confinement is the sound direction; certification is not.

**Among states where NEITHER player can force unconditional life, the large majority are DECISIVE, not drawn — so 'nobody can force life' is not a draw-pruning oracle.** Decisive fraction of the neither-can-force class: 12.9% (2x2, 124), 39.8% (3x2, 608), 57.8% (3x3, 12,804), 70.7% (4x3, 315,762), **85.3% (4x4, 22,885,430 states: 19,518,338 decisive vs 885,840 draw-by-loop)**. This REFUTES the pruning-oracle framing that was carried in T394's brief and echoed once in its own doc: a search that stopped valuing wherever neither player can force life would abandon 19.5 million decisively-valued 4x4 states. Cuts AGAINST the operator's territory-denial hypothesis: territory-denial does not explain those wins.
